summary_en: This phase 1 trial tests pressurized intraperitoneal aerosolized chemotherapy (PIPAC) with nab-paclitaxel in patients with pancreatic adenocarcinoma that has spread to the peritoneum. Nab-paclitaxel is delivered into the abdomen during a laparoscopic procedure and stays in contact with the peritoneum for 30 minutes, with up to three procedures given every six weeks. The main stated aim is to confirm the safety of PIPAC with nab-paclitaxel.
summary_es: Este ensayo de fase 1 evalúa la quimioterapia aerosolizada intraperitoneal presurizada (PIPAC) con nab-paclitaxel en pacientes con adenocarcinoma de páncreas que se ha diseminado al peritoneo. El nab-paclitaxel se administra en la cavidad abdominal durante un procedimiento laparoscópico y permanece en contacto con el peritoneo durante 30 minutos, con hasta tres procedimientos cada seis semanas. El objetivo principal indicado es confirmar la seguridad de PIPAC con nab-paclitaxel.
who_for: Adults 18 or older with pancreatic adenocarcinoma and suspected or confirmed peritoneal spread.
ECOG performance status of 2 or better.
Blood counts, liver tests and kidney function within the limits listed in the record.
Peritoneal disease visible on cross-sectional imaging or diagnostic laparoscopy.
Laparoscopy shows feasible access, room for aerosol, no impending bowel obstruction, under 5 L ascites, and not a candidate for cytoreduction and HIPEC.
not_for: Confirmed or suspected spread outside the peritoneum.
Bowel obstruction needing a feeding tube or total parenteral nutrition.
Life expectancy under 4 months, or prior intra-abdominal aerosol chemotherapy.
Prior anaphylactic reaction to nab-paclitaxel, or ascites over 5 L.
Uncontrolled illness, immune compromise, other investigational agents, or pregnancy.
